  PROBLEM: The awk slug-extraction pattern does not strip a `task_gap` prefix because `[a-z]*` does not match the underscore, leaving `task_gap <reviewer_slug>` and causing the roster check to falsely report a missing reviewer.
  WHY: The reported roster mismatch can make failed-slot verification fail and block auto-merge; severity differed between MAJOR and BLOCKER, so BLOCKER is retained. Minimax, Qwen, and GLM disputed the finding, stating that the ledger parser emits only `clean` and `failed` block kinds.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:367 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The awk slug-extraction command `sub(/^[a-z]* /, "")` does not match underscores in the block-type prefix. When the ledger contains a `task_gap` block (e.g. `task_gap minimax_minimax-m3`), the regex `[a-z]*` matches only "task", the underscore breaks the match, and `sub` does nothing. The extracted slug remains `task_gap minimax_minimax-m3` instead of `minimax_minimax-m3`. The roster check at line 385 then fails to match this malformed slug against the runner roster, emitting a false-positive `::warning::` that the ledger omits the reviewer and setting `claude_fixer_failed_slots_verified="false"` — even though the ledger correctly covers all reviewers.
  WHY: With `claude_fixer_failed_slots_verified="false"`, the quorum check at line 395-396 fails. The round hands off instead of auto-merging. Every review with a failed slot where the summariser produces a `task_gap` block hits this false positive. The identical pre-existing awk at line 293 has the same regex weakness, though that is a duplicate-detection check (false negative, not blocker) and predates this PR.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:361 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The awk slug-extraction pattern `sub(/^[a-z]* /, "")` does not correctly remove the "task_gap" classification prefix because `[a-z]*` does not match the underscore in "task_gap".
  WHY: The regex fails to strip the "task_gap" prefix from the ledger line, resulting in an extracted slug of "task_gap <reviewer_slug>" instead of just "<reviewer_slug>". The subsequent check `if [[ $'\n'"${claude_fixer_roster_ledger_slugs}"$'\n' != *$'\n'"${claude_fixer_roster_slug}"$'\n'* ]]` fails to match the slug, triggering a false "ledger omits reviewer" warning and unnecessary round hand-off, blocking auto-merge even when the ledger is actually complete.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "89 tests, including the mawk and gawk run" as stated in the PR description, and the claim that the new ledger-extraction logic in the roster check is covered by both `mawk` and `gawk`.
  Expected change site: tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py
  Evidence of absence: The new logic in scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:361 uses a new `awk` extraction pattern (`'$1 == "failed" { print $2; next } { sub(/^[a-z]* /, ""); print }'`). The PR tests do not explicitly re-run this roster check logic under both `mawk` and `gawk`. While the existing Python tests run the bash script, they do not verify that the logic holds specifically across both `awk` implementations, which can have subtle differences.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Make the scope (failed-slot ledgers only) and the "It then takes the same clean path" referent unambiguous in agents.md and the script header.
  Expected change site: agents.md:117 and scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:24-30, 43-50, 144-150.
  Evidence of absence: The added sentence describes failure conditions (omitted slot, empty roster, bad slug → warning), but the subsequent "It then takes the same clean path" uses an ambiguous pronoun ("It"), requiring the reader to backtrack to infer that "It" refers to the rule passing case. Similarly, the script-header comment at lines 24-30 jumps between describing the ledger block requirement and the runner-output guarantee without re-stating the successful roster case.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "89 tests, including the mawk and gawk run" per the PR description and "checks: bash -n, shellcheck, the Claude-fixer and file-size tests (72 passed, mawk), the Claude-fixer tests under gawk 5.2.1 (70 passed)" per the plan. The new roster check at scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:367 introduces a new awk invocation `awk '$1 == "failed" { print $2; next } { sub(/^[a-z]* /, ""); print }'` that does not run under the existing mawk/gawk parameterization.
  Expected change site: tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py — the existing test at lines 1048-1071 only parameterises the runner-output awk (lines 174-236), not the new ledger-extraction awk at line 367 or the pre-existing duplicate-check awk at line 293.
  Evidence of absence: No test in this PR drives the new line-367 awk through both `mawk` and `gawk` to confirm the `sub(/^[a-z]* /, "")` pattern behaves identically. The new awk is structurally identical to line 293 (which also is not under mawk/gawk coverage), so behavioural divergence is unlikely today, but the PR's "mawk and gawk run" claim is not borne out by the tests shipped: the only awk actually exercised under both implementations is the `claude_fixer_runner_output_state` one.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: agents.md Claude-fixer paragraph and the matching script-header comment block must make the scope (failed-slot ledgers only) and the success-transition unambiguous, so a reader does not have to backtrack to infer that "It then takes the same clean path" refers to the ledger-passing case rather than one of the named failure conditions.
  Expected change site: agents.md:117 and scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:24-30, 43-50, 144-150.
  Evidence of absence: agents.md:116-119 reads "an omitted slot, an empty roster, or an unexpected slot name hands off with a `::warning::`. It then takes the same clean path and logs `CLAUDE_FIXER_CLEAN_WITH_FAILED_SLOTS …`." The "It" follows three failure conditions and is ambiguous between "the rule" (passing case) and one of the failure conditions. The script header at lines 24-30, 43-50, and 144-150 ends with the new roster condition immediately followed by the clean-path statement, leaving the same gap: a reader has to backtrack to know "It" means the ledger passed the new check. Issue #5297 is the only reason the new check exists; the document should make the scope (failed-slot ledgers only, AD-1) explicit at the transition.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:391-394
  Issue: The warning message reads "Claude-fixer reviewer roster is empty (no status_review_<slug>.txt or review_<slug>.txt in PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR); the ledger is not clean." but the same branch also fires when PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR is unset or is not a directory, in which case "in PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR" is misleading.
  Suggested minimal fix: distinguish the unset / not-a-directory case from the empty directory case with a separate warning, e.g. emit one warning when `[ -z "${PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR:-}" ] || [ ! -d "${PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR}" ]` and keep the existing message only when the directory exists but is empty. Three lines.
  Estimated lines changed: 3
